agree.reason: The hook quoting her own $600K figure and the 'sits on top of your WMS' line make a 20-minute call plausible, but nothing connects the result to her money or tells her what her IT director would actually have to do, so the reader who resists has little reason to say yes.

honest.reason: Every number comes from the brief, and the draft rightly drops the 'cut errors in half' claim in favour of one named result, but it shows only the best of six customers and leaves out the 2.8-to-2.2 case, which hints at a wider pattern than the facts support.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are left raw: the draft never says this was a 54% drop, never puts that against her $600K (roughly $300K if returns fall in line), and never sets it against the cost of about $75K a year for five sites.

right_comparison.reason: The $600K yearly loss is named in the opening and then dropped, so the cost of doing nothing is never set against the cost of the product.

qualification.reason: One customer's result is offered as the whole proof, with no hedge she could check, such as a one-site pilot with a target error rate by a stated month and what happens if it misses.

objections.reason: Saying it doesn't replace the WMS partly answers the IT director's likely veto, but the draft doesn't say how much IT work setup needs or whether it touches the WMS at all, and price, which the brief supplies, is left out.

fit.reason: It's short, made of brief paragraphs, easy to read on a phone and ends with a clear ask, as the brief requested.
